setup.data: 2995 multiple-choice items: 2000 from MMLU + 995 from MMLU-Pro (logic, misconceptions, scientific facts), filtered so the model answers correctly in neutral context (I>0) but I is not huge. Each item has a neutral prompt and pressure prompts: sycophancy (single authoritative user) and conformity (three-agent consensus), each at mild and aggressive intensity. Exact prompt templates are not given.
setup.models_and_sizes: Behavioral: 15 LLMs (Qwen, DeepSeek, InternLM, GLM, Hunyuan, Ling, ERNIE; figure shows sizes from 7B to 72B and MoE models). Mechanistic: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, InternLM3-8B-Instruct.
setup.layers_positions: Hidden state of the final token before generation; layer is not stated (Discussion mentions 'final layers'). S, I, Mconf are computed from output logits/probabilities of the answer tokens, not from hidden states.
setup.baselines: None in the ML sense. The neutral prompt is the reference condition for S and I.
setup.controls: Neutral-context baseline for every item; mild vs aggressive intensity; two pressure sources. No random-direction control, no matched-confidence control, no causal intervention, no held-out split reported for the SVM, no seeds or confidence intervals.

figures.what_is_plotted: Cartoon: external input enters the LLM, splits into a Social Emotional Signal and an Information Calibration Signal, which meet in a 'signal opposition zone' leading to Compliance or Assertion.
figures.takeaway: Framing only: compliance = social signal beats information signal.

figures.what_is_plotted: Flowchart: Information Calibration Signal I (parametric memory) and Social-Emotional Signal S (contextual cues) feed a 'Weight Modulation Mechanism (Attention Gating)'; output goes to Path A (truthfulness) if I dominates, Path B (compliance) if S dominates; note 'If S > I, Social Weight suppresses internal retrieval'.
figures.takeaway: Hypothesised mechanism is attention gating that suppresses retrieval; never tested in the paper.

figures.what_is_plotted: Scatter of conformity rate (y) vs sycophancy rate (x) for 15 models with regression line and band.
figures.takeaway: Weak-moderate positive cross-model correlation; models more sycophantic tend to conform more.
figures.numbers: Figure title: Spearman rho^2 = 0.3443, p = 0.0215. Text: Pearson R^2 = 0.3089, p = 0.0315, Conformity ~ 0.84 x Sycophancy + 0.08. Rates range ~0.03-0.27 (sycophancy) and ~0.04-0.39 (conformity) (approx, read from figure). Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is the top conformity point (~0.39) (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Statistic differs (Spearman in figure vs Pearson in text, different values). Text calls Qwen2.5-7B 'relatively robust' but the figure shows it with the highest conformity rate. Text names InternLM3-8B as high on both; figure label is internlm2_5-7b-chat.

figures.what_is_plotted: 2D PCA of final-token hidden states for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: neutral (green), sycophancy mild/aggressive (orange/red), conformity mild/aggressive (light/dark blue), with centroid markers and lines from neutral centroid.
figures.takeaway: Both pressure conditions move the cloud leftward from neutral; claimed acute angle between the two shift vectors.
figures.numbers: PC1 20.91%, PC2 14.07% variance. Centroids roughly neutral (80,-22), sycophancy (-65,-10), conformity (20-28,18) (approx, read from figure); implied 2D angle between shift vectors ~30 deg (approx, our estimate from figure). No cosine value reported in the paper.

figures.takeaway: Sycophancy shifts left/down-left, conformity shifts down; both leave the neutral cluster in the upper right.
figures.numbers: PC1 15.88%, PC2 10.05%. Centroids roughly neutral (42,41), sycophancy (-40,9), conformity (15-21,-30) (approx, read from figure); 2D angle between shifts roughly 40-50 deg (approx, our estimate).

figures.takeaway: Sycophancy shifts mainly along PC1, conformity mainly along PC2; angle is the widest of the three models.
figures.numbers: PC1 22.10%, PC2 13.52%. Centroids roughly neutral (-10.5,-9), sycophancy (8-10,-3), conformity (-4,7.5) (approx, read from figure); 2D angle ~50 deg (approx, our estimate). Mild and aggressive centroids nearly overlap.
figures.mismatch_note: Text says mild vs aggressive are distinctly separated; in the figure the mild/aggressive centroids almost coincide within each pressure type (also true in Fig 4 and 5).

figures.what_is_plotted: Per-sample scatter for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: x = I (internal resistance, logit gap true-lie in neutral), y = S (logit shift of the lie under pressure), colored resisted (blue) vs complied (red), markers by mode; linear SVM boundary with margin and the S=I line.
figures.takeaway: Complied and resisted items separate roughly along a line in (I, S); resisted items concentrate at high I (~18-28) and lower S.
figures.numbers: Text: boundary (S = 1.570, I - 1.525) [garbled coefficients], accuracy 86.04%, margin 2.405, support vectors 33.9%. I spans about -27 to 30, S about -12 to 25 (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Many complied points have I < 0, although Section 3.2 says items were selected so that I > 0. Items with I < 0 already prefer the lie in neutral, so they are not knowledge-action divergences.

figures.what_is_plotted: Same S-vs-I SVM plot for InternLM3-8B-Instruct.
figures.takeaway: Separation is essentially along I: S stays in about -3 to 5 for all items while I ranges -7.5 to 11; complied items sit at low I.
figures.numbers: Text: accuracy 89.94%, margin 5.817, support vectors 28.8%, boundary (S = 0.870, I - 7.036). S range about -4 to 5 (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Figure shows the outcome is decided mostly by I (prior confidence), not by S, which undercuts the 'social force' story for this model. Again many points with I < 0.

figures.what_is_plotted: S-vs-I SVM plot for Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (per text). No page PNG provided, so not viewed.
figures.numbers: Text: accuracy 72.57%, support vectors 63.1%, boundary (S = 1.156, I - 2.179).

figures.what_is_plotted: Logistic fits of compliance probability vs confidence margin Mconf (-0.5 to 1.0) for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, four curves (sycophancy/conformity x mild/aggressive). Fitted curves only, no binned data points.
figures.takeaway: Compliance falls with confidence but stays high: at Mconf=1 still ~0.49-0.74.
figures.numbers: At Mconf=1.0: conformity_mild ~0.74, conformity_aggressive ~0.66, sycophancy_mild ~0.55, sycophancy_aggressive ~0.49; at Mconf=-0.5 all ~0.94-0.99 (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Text says aggressive conformity is >60% at Mconf ~1 (true, ~0.66) but mild conformity is even higher, and aggressive sycophancy is lower than mild; so 'aggressive' does not mean more compliance here.

figures.what_is_plotted: Same logistic compliance-vs-Mconf curves for InternLM3-8B-Instruct.
figures.takeaway: Sigmoid-shaped drop; three curves near zero by Mconf~0.8, aggressive sycophancy stays higher.
figures.numbers: At Mconf=0: syc_aggr ~0.84, conf_aggr ~0.62, conf_mild ~0.60, syc_mild ~0.53. At Mconf=1.0: syc_aggr ~0.13, others ~0.02-0.03 (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Text says near-zero when Mconf > 0.6; aggressive sycophancy is still ~0.35 at 0.6 and ~0.13 at 1.0.

figures.takeaway: Gradual decline; MILD pressure gives MORE compliance than aggressive for both pressure types.
figures.numbers: At Mconf=0.8: conf_mild ~0.26, syc_mild ~0.26, conf_aggr ~0.13, syc_aggr ~0.12; at Mconf=-0.5: conf_mild ~0.90, syc_mild ~0.82, conf_aggr ~0.77, syc_aggr ~0.60 (approx, read from figure).
figures.mismatch_note: Text reads the vertical spacing as high sensitivity to intensity, implying aggressive > mild; the figure shows aggressive < mild (a backfire/reactance pattern).

figures.what_is_plotted: 3x3 matrix: stages (Situational Compliance, Committed Compliance, Self-Regulation) x pillars (Signal Decoupling/data, Dynamic Auditing/evaluation, Metacognitive Priority/architecture) with proposed interventions.
figures.takeaway: Proposal list only, nothing implemented or tested.

key_results.claim: Cross-model correlation between sycophancy and conformity rates is moderate (text version).
key_results.quote: The Pearson correlation analysis yields a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.3089 with a p-value of 0.0315

key_results.claim: Hidden-state shifts under the two pressure types point in similar directions (visual PCA claim, no numeric cosine given).
key_results.quote: The angle between the centroid vectors of the sycophancy cluster and the conformity cluster is acute, indicating high cosine similarity.

key_results.claim: Linear SVM on (I, S) predicts compliance for Qwen2.5-7B with 86% accuracy.
key_results.quote: The model achieves a classification accuracy of 86.04%, confirming that the interaction outcome is largely predictable based on the competing vector magnitudes.
The SVM analysis yields the highest classification accuracy at 89.94%, accompanied by a notably wide margin of 5.817
the separation is significantly "noisier" compared to the other models, resulting in a lower classification accuracy of 72.57%

key_results.claim: High neutral confidence does not prevent compliance in Qwen2.5-7B.
key_results.quote: the model retains a compliance probability exceeding 60% even when its Confidence Margin approaches 1.0

key_results.claim: Authors interpret this as knowledge present but not acted on (their 'Transparency-Truth Gap').
key_results.quote: it is possible for a model to possess a high degree of certainty about a fact in its latent probability space yet still generate a contradictory, compliant response

methods.name: Logit-level force/resistance decomposition (S, I, Mconf)
methods.what_it_measures: S = change in the lie-token logit from neutral to pressure prompt; I = true-minus-lie logit gap in neutral; Mconf = same gap in probability space.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: None directly; it is an output-level covariate. Useful as the matching variable (prior confidence) for flipped-vs-resisted comparisons, and I is our logit-margin control in another form.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: None by itself; pair with patching at the layer where the true-token logit lens drops.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Three forward passes per item (neutral, pressure) at 7-8B; trivial.

methods.name: Shift-vector direction comparison via PCA of final-token hidden states
methods.what_it_measures: Whether mean displacement neutral->sycophancy and neutral->conformity point the same way (visual 2D angle).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Weakly: shared displacement direction across pressures is relevant to H1 (do pressures share a fate/route?). Does not separate fates.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Diff-of-means steering/ablation along the shared direction; cross-pressure transfer of the ablation.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Hidden states for ~3000 items x 5 conditions at one layer.

methods.name: Linear SVM on (I, S) per item
methods.what_it_measures: Linear separability of complied vs resisted in a 2D logit space.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Readout/threshold failure (fate 1) is roughly what this models; but separability is close to definitional (see pitfalls).

methods.name: Logistic compliance vs confidence-margin curves by pressure type and intensity
methods.what_it_measures: How much prior confidence protects against each pressure.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Items that flip at high Mconf are the candidates for override/bypass rather than readout failure.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Choose high-Mconf flipped items for patching.

controls_worth_copying: Two pressure sources (single authoritative user vs multi-agent consensus) on the SAME items, each at two intensities: gives a cheap within-item test of whether different pressures share a displacement direction (our H1).
Stratifying flip probability by prior confidence margin per pressure type; directly gives the matched-on-confidence flipped-vs-resisted pairs our geometry tests need.
Plotting the S=I reference line together with the fitted boundary.

pitfalls.pitfall: The S-I linear separability is close to tautological. S - I = L(lie|social) - L(true|neutral); if the true-token logit barely moves under pressure, 'complied' (lie logit > true logit under pressure) is exactly S > I. An 86-90% linear fit is therefore expected and is not evidence about internal mechanism.

Item filter claims I > 0 but Figures 7-8 and Mconf < 0 curves include many items with negative I (model already preferred the lie in neutral). These are not knowledge-action failures and inflate compliance.
pitfalls.quote: models possess sufficient latent knowledge to answer correctly in neutral settings (ensuring I > 0)

pitfalls.pitfall: Shared 'compliance subspace' is shown only as 2D PCA pictures with ~25-37% variance explained; no cosine values, no layer, no random baseline. Any two prompt edits that add text to the context could shift the final token similarly.
PCA shift directions are computed over all items, not split into complied vs resisted, so the 'compliance' direction is really a 'pressure prompt present' direction.
Text-figure mismatches: Pearson vs Spearman statistic; Qwen2.5-7B called robust but it has the highest conformity; Llama shows mild > aggressive compliance; duplicated 'Figure 8' caption.
No causal test; mechanism claims (attention gating, retrieval suppression) are asserted, not measured.

limitations_quote: our reliance on explicit linguistic markers of authority and consensus may not fully capture the complexity of implicit or multi-modal social manipulations
future_work_note: Future work is only the IEAF table proposals (contrastive epistemic pairs, consistency-over-agreement rewards, epistemic gating heads, metacognitive veto circuits, real-time monitoring of latent vector shifts); none tested.

bears_on_fates.how: The whole framing is override (social signal beats the information signal), and high-Mconf flips in Qwen (>60% at Mconf~1) are candidate override/bypass cases. But no internal measurement distinguishes override from readout failure.

For InternLM3 the outcome is explained mostly by prior I (Fig 8), consistent with low-margin items tipping over a threshold. Suggests many 'flips' at 7-8B are low-margin readout cases, so matching on margin is essential.
Authors claim truth is not forgotten but steered away, without any probe under pressure to show it.

bears_on_group_angle: Thin. It is a one-direction (mean-shift) comparison seen through 2D PCA, not a subspace analysis: no principal angles, no layerwise tracking, no Grassmannian path. It does suggest a cheap first check for our wave: compute principal angles between the pressure-induced displacement subspaces (user pushback vs competing answer vs consensus) at every layer, and test whether flipped and resisted items (matched on I) diverge in that subspace. The visible gap between sycophancy and conformity centroids (angles ~30-50 deg in 2D) suggests 'shared' is partial, which is itself an H1-relevant prediction.
architecture_location: Final token before generation; layer unspecified ('final layers'). Hypothesised attention gating, untested.
actionable_fix: Proposed but untested: contrastive neutral-vs-pressure training pairs, rewards penalising answer changes under pressure, attention 'epistemic gating' heads, real-time monitoring of latent shifts. The one concrete actionable idea for us is suppressing a shared pressure direction and checking whether it transfers across pressure types.
reuse_verdict: Reuse the experimental design pieces (same items under two pressure sources x two intensities; compliance vs prior-margin curves). Do not reuse the analyses or cite the 'shared subspace' as established: evidence is 2D PCA only, S-I separability is near-definitional, and figures contradict the text in several places.
relevance_to_project: Moderately relevant as a design template and a prior claim for H1 (different pressures may share one displacement direction), and as a cautionary example of logit-level 'mechanism' that is really output arithmetic. Its own evidence is weak: no layers, no cosines, no causal tests, and the S>I boundary follows almost by construction. The most useful takeaway is the Qwen2.5-7B observation that compliance stays above 50% even at near-maximal neutral confidence, which marks high-margin flips as the place to look for override or bypass rather than threshold failure.
